review_state: PARTIAL; REM-016 harness source/test statically reviewed; runtime migration harness, image override provenance, lock timeout, interruption cleanup, disposable target approval, complete inventory and independent critique remain open

paths_reviewed.review_notes: The harness pins a default PostgreSQL image digest, generates per-run container/database identifiers, publishes only a dynamic loopback port, strips ambient DB URL/PG variables from migration children, uses fixed URLs for owned per-run databases, inserts synthetic accounts, and drops DBs/removes container in finally. Output is repo-relative, exclusive-create, mode 0600. It exercises install/reexecution, prefix-to-head upgrade, advisory lock, pg_dump/restore into a replacement DB, checksum failure/recovery, and unknown target. No harness execution occurred.

The test reads the harness, package manifest, and CI workflow as text and asserts pinned image/default isolation markers, scenario names, and package/CI wiring. It does not import/execute Docker, PostgreSQL, migration code, or output writing; this is a static contract only.

test_execution.environment: The contract ran under the standalone SPA Vitest/JSDOM config, without a database global setup. It only reads source/config files. The source was syntax-checked but not imported or executed. No Docker, database, provider, or network operation occurred.
test_execution.runtime_harness: NOT RUN: it starts Docker, creates/drops PostgreSQL databases, executes migrations and writes optional output. No disposable runtime target was authorized for this round.

boundary_review.database_isolation: Migration subprocess environment deletes ambient DATABASE_URL/DATABASE_URL_TEST/MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL/E2E_DATABASE_URL and PG connection keys, then sets URLs constructed from the harness-owned container and per-run DB names. Port binding is 127.0.0.1 with dynamic host port.
boundary_review.data_scope: Only synthetic account rows and migration-ledger checks are authored by this harness; the report explicitly disclaims target rollback, RPO/RTO, independently built historical application compatibility, and production data use.
boundary_review.cleanup: Ordinary errors/success pass through finally that drops created databases and force-removes the named container; rollback dump temp files are removed in finally. Cleanup failures are best-effort and do not replace the scenario failure.
boundary_review.output: Output path is constrained to repository-relative paths and opened with wx and mode 0600; CI output path is fixed under artifacts/operations and upload retention is 30 days.

findings_and_limits.observation: Default image is digest-pinned, but MIGRATION_HARNESS_IMAGE may replace it with any string containing @sha256:. The harness does not allowlist the digest/registry and Docker network egress is not disabled. The edited CI workflow does not set the override, but an ambient override could select arbitrary image code.
findings_and_limits.required_followup: Restrict the override to an approved image digest/registry or remove the override before relying on this as a controlled local harness.

findings_and_limits.observation: spawnMigration starts the lock-probe migration with spawn and no timeout. runLockProbe awaits migration.promise after unlocking; if that child never exits, the await can hang before finally reaches the SIGTERM cleanup.
findings_and_limits.required_followup: Add a bounded child completion timeout/cancellation path and await cleanup, then test timeout/release behavior in an approved disposable container.

findings_and_limits.observation: The database/container cleanup is in finally for normal async completion/failure, but no explicit SIGINT/SIGTERM handler is installed for the harness process. Abrupt interruption may leave its named container or database behind; cleanup commands also intentionally swallow failure.
findings_and_limits.required_followup: Define and verify interruption cleanup, including safe recovery for containers left by a killed process.

findings_and_limits.observation: The focused contract test asserts text markers and wiring; it does not execute Docker, verify actual ambient-variable isolation, perform migrations, assert cleanup, test image trust, or check report output permissions. node --check only establishes syntax.
findings_and_limits.required_followup: Treat the 3/3 contract as static evidence only; require a separately approved disposable-runtime verification for migration, rollback/replacement restore and cleanup claims.

findings_and_limits.observation: The rollback scenario restores a pg_dump into a newly created replacement database and compares prefix ledger/data. It does not test an in-place migration downgrade or certify production restore/RPO/RTO; the source report states these limits.
findings_and_limits.required_followup: Keep production rollback/restore and RPO/RTO under REM-024/M-14 authority and evidence.

candidate_actions.hold_reason: Source hashes and focused static contract are verified, but the default image override boundary, lock-child liveness, interruption cleanup and runtime database behavior remain unresolved and were not executed.
